title: The epigenetics of color swatches: histone deacetylation regulates green coloration in Chrysanthemum
content: Fruits and flowers exhibit a wide variety of vibrant colors, whereas foliar tissues are predominantly green. The role of color in plants extends beyond their aesthetics, as colors in fruits and flowers are important for attracting seed dispersers and pollinators. A balance of chlorophyll and carotenoids, along with other pigments such as anthocyanins, dictates the final color of the flower, fruits and leaves. In leaves, colors are regulated by Golden2-like (GLK) transcription factors, which regulate the expression of enzymes controlling chlorophyll and carotenoid production. Apart from “color swatch” control, the GLK transcription factors are essential in regulating chloroplast development and senescence (Qin et al. 2021). Interestingly, chlorophyll and carotenoid accumulation in fruit is GLK-independent, with other factors such as CAROTENOID CLEAVAGE DIOXYGENASE 4 (CCD4) coordinating color (Amaya et al. 2025; Han et al. 2016). However, the precise mechanisms for color regulation in flowers are largely unknown.
